text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- A week after deposing his senior rival in two days of bloody fighting, Cambodia's Second Prime Minister Hun Sen says the country must have a free and fair election.
- Singapore businessmen are holding back their investments in Cambodia and hoping the political situation there will be back to normal very soon.
- Mail services to Cambodia suspended until further notice.

- One-off 10 percent rebate in last Friday's Budget statement better for Singaporeans than a one percentage point cut in personal income tax rates, Trade and Industry and Second Finance Minister Lee Yock Suan says.

- Twelve-year-old Australian girl dies and several people injured in Canberra when hospital demolition went wrong, spewing debris over thousands of spectators who turned out for what was billed a family event.
- New telephone on sale in Britain which can tell whether person on other end of line is telling truth, according to The Sunday Times.
- More Central Provident Fund members putting their retirement funds in life insurance policies sold under the new CPF Investment Scheme introduced this year.
- Hotelier Ong Beng Seng may be considering selling his Concorde Hotel at Havelock Road after refurbishment is completed, say sources.
- US dollar fetches 33 pesos in black market, 12 percent higher than banks' reference rate, an uncertainty swept Philippine currency, trading of which resumes today.
- Worldwide chip sales in May show year-on-year growth for the first time this year, but observers still holding breaths for clearer sign of recovery in key electronics sector here.
- Entrepreneur Gordon Wu proposes ambitious project to reclaim 10,700 hectares of land to house 3.6 million people in housing-short Hongkong.
- Homegrown Komoco Motors, vehicle distributorship owned by hotelier Ong Beng Seng and retailer Jopie Ong, will go public any time now.
- Keppel Corp proposes issue of redeemable convertible cumulative preference shares to raise US$350 million.
